claims.text: The Ta–Nb–Hf–Zr–Ti alloy is a five-element high-entropy alloy.
The Ta–Nb–Hf–Zr–Ti alloy has a body-centered-cubic lattice.
The constituent elements are randomly distributed on crystallographic sites.
The Ta–Nb–Hf–Zr–Ti HEA exhibits zero-resistance superconductivity from ambient pressure to approximately 190 GPa.
The alloy undergoes no structural phase transition over the reported pressure range up to about 190 GPa.
Atomic-level configurational disorder governs the robustness of superconductivity in high-entropy alloys.
Configurational disorder modifies the phonon density of states by softening or broadening phonon modes.
The disorder-modified phonon spectrum enhances electron–phonon coupling.
Enhanced electron–phonon coupling stabilizes Cooper pairing under extreme pressure.
Prolonged annealing or a composition change can reduce mixing entropy and promote local ordering in the comparison sample.
The more disordered HEA will have a higher superconducting transition temperature than an ordered, lower-entropy analog.
The more disordered HEA will retain zero-resistance superconductivity over a broader pressure range than the ordered analog.
An ordered analog will show a lower or more rapidly pressure-degraded transition temperature.
The proposed disorder mechanism dominates only in single-phase HEAs with a bcc or similarly simple lattice when configurational disorder is the primary differentiator.
Phase separation or multiple phases can introduce additional mechanisms that obscure the effect of configurational disorder.
Comparable transition temperatures and pressure resilience in the disordered and ordered samples would falsify the proposed governing role of configurational disorder.
